title: Pokemon SoulGold (v1.1.4 to 1.2.1)
sources: The ROM itself (SoulGold 1.1.4, 1.2 and 1.2.1, pokeemerald-expansion 1.15 builds; their map sections are 16-bit): region map section names (each place resolves to a section with maps), trainer names, teams and levels (Classic and Hard teams) and the item and move evolution methods, read on the PC with throwaway tools
GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold: README (features, optional level caps) and release notes
pokemonsoulgold.com: changelog, about page, gift Pokémon guide
soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs): FAQ, walkthrough, starters, legendaries; romhackguides.com (1.1.2)

SoulGold official docs (eemeliri.github.io/soulgold, v1.2.1): FAQ, legendary locations, gift and trade Pokémon, trophy milestones, hidden grottos, shiny hunting; the trainers and items data (locations)
soulgold.run: changelog (v1.2 of 3 Oct 2026, v1.2.1 of 25 Oct 2026) and FAQ; GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold release 1.2.1
Bulbapedia: Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver walkthrough (the story beats SoulGold keeps from HGSS)

milestones.name: A starter from Elm's case
milestones.tips: Nine starters: Chikorita, Chespin, Sprigatito; Cyndaquil, Fennekin, Torchic; Totodile, Froakie, Popplio. Gold (or Crystal), a second trainer from New Bark, battles you with a Lv 4 Marill. Cherrygrove gives an Alolan Rattata or a Galarian Zigzagoon once you have Poké Balls.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

milestones.name: Rival: the passerby in Cherrygrove
milestones.tips: A passerby (the rival, shown as ??? until you learn his name) battles you with a lone Lv 5 Chikorita, Cyndaquil or Totodile. He also hands you the Exp. Share before you reach Violet City.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Cherrygrove City); SoulGold docs: items (Exp. Share)

milestones.name: Route Expert Nate
milestones.tips: The first of five optional Route Experts: Alolan Geodude and Mareep (Lv 8). Water and Grass moves handle the Geodude.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers; SoulGold docs: FAQ (Route Experts)

milestones.name: Elder Li in Sprout Tower
milestones.tips: Natu, Ralts and Bellsprout (Lv 9-10) at the top of Sprout Tower. As in HGSS, beating him earns Flash. After the eighth badge he waits for you again; then the tower's basement holds Marshadow.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; Bulbapedia: HGSS walkthrough (Sprout Tower); SoulGold docs: legendary locations (Marshadow)

milestones.name: Gym 1: Falkner
milestones.badge_note: Zephyr Badge. Optional level cap after it: 19.
milestones.tips: Flying types: Pidgey, Gligar, Pidgeotto (Lv 11-12). Electric, Ice and Rock moves. Hard mode has its own teams (often a level higher, gyms as double battles).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold README and releases

milestones.name: Rocket Eto in Slowpoke Well
milestones.tips: A named grunt with a Lv 17 Sandile on B1F; you meet him again in the Mahogany hideout and under Goldenrod. Water, Grass or Fighting moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Slowpoke Well B1F)

milestones.name: Team Rocket: Proton in Slowpoke Well
milestones.tips: Proton: Nosepass, Houndour, Porygon (Lv 17-18). Fighting moves; Ground for Nosepass and Houndour.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gym 2: Bugsy
milestones.badge_note: Hive Badge. Optional level cap after it: 26.
milestones.tips: Bug types: Scyther, Whirlipede, Cutiefly (Lv 19-20). Fire, Flying and Rock moves. Hard mode has its own teams (often a level higher, gyms as double battles).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold README and releases

milestones.name: Rival: first battles
milestones.tips: The rival (Silver in the sources) fights you several times; his early team is Haunter, Pawniard, Pidgeotto and his starter at Lv 20-22 (21-22 on Hard). He also gives the Odd Egg (Bagon, Gible, Feebas, Riolu, Jangmo-o, Hisuian Zorua or Goomy). The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the levels are the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; pokemonsoulgold.com (changelog, gift Pokémon)

milestones.name: Gold or Crystal on Route 34
milestones.tips: Gold or Crystal again: Zorua, Oricorio, Azumarill (Lv 22-23).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Route Expert Kiana
milestones.tips: Breloom, Lycanroc and Cinccino (Lv 26). Flying moves beat Breloom; Fighting and Steel handle the other two.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers; SoulGold docs: FAQ (Route Experts)

milestones.name: Gym 3: Whitney
milestones.badge_note: Plain Badge. The Battle Factory opens after this gym.
milestones.tips: Normal types: Audino, Girafarig, Miltank (Lv 25-27). Fighting moves. Her gym opens after the quiz on Radio Tower 1F. Hard mode has its own teams (often a level higher, gyms as double battles).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Rival: Burned Tower
milestones.tips: Floatzel or Haunter, Pawniard, Staravia, a Lampent/Weepinbell/Clodsire and his starter's middle stage at Lv 30-33. The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the levels are the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Burned Tower 1F)

milestones.name: Gym 4: Morty
milestones.tips: Ghost types: Corsola, Doublade, Misdreavus, Gengar (Lv 33-34). Dark and Ghost moves. After the Burned Tower, Raikou, Entei and Suicune roam. Hard mode has its own teams (often a level higher, gyms as double battles).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold README and releases

milestones.name: Gym: Chuck
milestones.tips: Fighting types: Hitmontop, Mienshao, Poliwrath, Annihilape (Lv 41-42). Psychic, Flying and Fairy moves. Chuck, Jasmine and Pryce scale with your badges: Lv 42 with four, 45 with five, 48 with six.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Eusine
milestones.tips: Golisopod, Wobbuffet, Magnezone (Lv 38-39).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table

milestones.name: Route Expert Vera
milestones.tips: Galarian Obstagoon, Alolan Muk, Gliscor and Heracross (Lv 43-44). Fairy for Obstagoon, Ground for Muk, Ice for Gliscor, Flying for Heracross.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers; SoulGold docs: FAQ (Route Experts)

milestones.name: Gym: Jasmine
milestones.tips: Steel types: Skarmory, Tinkaton, Magneton, Scizor, Steelix (Lv 44-45) at five badges. Fire, Fighting and Ground moves. Strength comes from the Olivine café.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gym: Pryce
milestones.badge_note: Glacier Badge. Optional level cap until the Rocket takeover: 55.
milestones.tips: Ice types: Ninetales, Mamoswine, Glaceon, Weavile, Froslass (Lv 47-48) at six badges. Fire, Fighting, Rock and Steel moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Karate King Kiyo in Mt. Mortar
milestones.tips: Hitmonlee, Hitmonchan and Hitmontop (Lv 42) on B1F. Beating him gives you a Tyrogue. Psychic, Flying and Fairy moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Mt Mortar B1F); SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

milestones.name: Route Expert Laurel
milestones.tips: Sceptile, Cradily, Hawlucha and Cloyster (Lv 45-46). Ice and Flying moves for the Grass types, Electric for Cloyster.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers; SoulGold docs: FAQ (Route Experts)

milestones.name: Rocket Eto in the hideout
milestones.tips: Eto again on B3F with a Lv 44 Krookodile: Water, Grass, Ice, Bug and Fighting moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Rocket Hideout B3F)

milestones.name: Rocket hideout in Mahogany
milestones.tips: Petrel (Scrafty, Persian, Pyroar, Weezing (Lv 47-48)) on B3F and Ariana (Arbok, Vileplume, Dragalge (Lv 48-49)) on B2F.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Rival: Goldenrod Underground
milestones.tips: During the Radio Tower takeover he battles you at the underground switches: Gengar or Floatzel, Bisharp, Staraptor, a Clodsire/Victreebel/Chandelure and his starter's final stage (Lv 48-49; 49-51 on Hard). The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the levels are the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Goldenrod City Underground Switches)

milestones.name: Rocket Eto under Goldenrod
milestones.tips: Eto's last stand in the underground storage: Krookodile and Rhyperior (Lv 48). Water and Grass moves hit both hard. The storage also holds Leftovers.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Goldenrod City Underground Storage); SoulGold docs: items

milestones.name: Team Rocket takes the Radio Tower
milestones.tips: Proton on 4F (Crobat, Farigiraf, Porygon-Z, Nidoking, Scrafty (Lv 49-51)), Petrel and Ariana on 5F (Scrafty, Rotom, Persian, Pyroar, Weezing (Lv 48-49); Arbok, Toxapex, Vileplume, Gyarados, Dragalge (Lv 50-51)), Archer at the top (Ninetales, Tauros, Marowak, Slowking, Houndoom (Lv 52-54)). The Mega Ring is yours afterwards, and you choose the Rainbow Wing or the Silver Wing.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gold or Crystal in the Ice Path
milestones.tips: Azumarill, Zoroark, Oricorio, Flygon, Ampharos (Lv 54-55; Hard adds Gogoat, Lv 56-58). The Ice Path also holds Waterfall, and the second Safari Zone area opens before you enter it.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: FAQ

milestones.name: Gym 8: Clair
milestones.badge_note: Rising Badge: Rock Climb (since 1.1). Optional cap until Ho-Oh or Lugia: 62, then 70 to the Champion.
milestones.tips: Dragons: Altaria, Gyarados, Dragonite, Hydrapple, Kingdra (Lv 57-58). Ice, Dragon and Fairy moves. Hard mode has its own teams (often a level higher, gyms as double battles).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Blaine at the Olivine port
milestones.tips: With eight badges, find Blaine inside the Olivine port: Ninetales, Cinderace, Ceruledge, Magmortar, Volcarona (Lv 60-61; Hard adds Emboar, Lv 62). Water, Rock and Ground moves. Beating him opens Faraway Island, home of Mew.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Olivine City Port); SoulGold docs: legendary locations (Mew)

milestones.name: The Kimono Girls
milestones.tips: Five battles in the Ecruteak Dance Theater, each an Eevee and one Eeveelution (Vaporeon, Flareon, Espeon, Jolteon, Umbreon) at Lv 60. Bring answers to all five types; Fighting moves cover Umbreon, Ghost and Dark cover Espeon.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Ecruteak City Theater)

milestones.name: Route Expert Anton
milestones.tips: Galarian Darmanitan, Tauros, Haxorus and Arcanine (Lv 63). Fire and Fairy cover most of it; Ice for Haxorus. Route 27 also gives a Choice Band.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers; SoulGold docs: FAQ (Route Experts)

milestones.name: Rival: Victory Road
milestones.tips: His final team at Lv 65 (66-67 on Hard): Gengar or Floatzel, Kingambit, Staraptor, a Clodsire/Victreebel/Chandelure, his starter's final stage and Eelektross, Armarouge or Haxorus. The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the levels are the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Victory Road 1F)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Will
milestones.tips: Farigiraf, Espeon, Slowbro, Reuniclus, Alakazam, Braviary (Lv 66-67). Dark, Ghost and Bug moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Koga
milestones.tips: Ariados, Roserade, Muk, Overqwil, Scolipede, Crobat (Lv 67-68). Psychic and Ground moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Bruno
milestones.tips: Hitmontop, Heracross, Staraptor, Annihilape, Kommo-o, Machamp (Lv 67-69). Psychic, Flying and Fairy moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Karen
milestones.tips: Grimmsnarl, Umbreon, Kingambit, Scrafty, Honchkrow, Absol (Lv 69-70). Fighting, Bug and Fairy moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Champion Lance
milestones.tips: Exeggutor, Dragonite, Baxcalibur, Hydrapple, Dragapult, Archaludon (Lv 69-71). Ice and Fairy moves; Archaludon is Steel/Dragon (Fighting, Ground).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gold or Crystal on Mt. Silver
milestones.tips: Iron Treads, Zoroark, Baxcalibur, Azumarill, Ampharos, Tangrowth (Lv 73-75; Hard has Iron Leaves, Lv 75-76) at the summit. Finishing this rival story gives Jirachi and starts the quest for Cresselia, Darkrai and HM Dive.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: legendary locations

milestones.name: Elite Four rematch
milestones.tips: The Elite Four return at Lv 85, each with two possible teams (Karen's second is Ghost-heavy: Sableye, Gengar, Chandelure, Mimikyu, Aegislash, Dragapult). After them comes a Title Defense instead of Lance alone.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers; soulgold.run changelog (v1.2)

milestones.name: Title Defense
milestones.tips: After the rematched Elite Four a challenger defends against you: Lance (Lv 86), Steven (86), Leaf (87) or a Johto leader at Lv 85 with a legend in the team (Falkner Landorus, Bugsy Genesect, Whitney Regigigas, Morty Giratina, Chuck Galarian Zapdos, Jasmine Dialga, Pryce Articuno, Clair Rayquaza). A round also respawns the Paradox legends (since 1.2).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Title Defense); soulgold.run changelog (v1.2)

milestones.name: Gym rematches
milestones.tips: The leaders wait at new places with Lv 76-81 teams (78-84 on Hard): Falkner at the Violet school, Bugsy in the National Park, Whitney on Dept. Store 6F, Morty on the Bellchime Trail, Chuck on the Route 47 bridge, Jasmine in the Olivine café, Pryce at the Lake of Rage, Clair in the Dragon's Den. Beat them all for Victini (the old woman in the Kitakami Border house).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: FAQ; SoulGold docs: legendary locations

milestones.name: Steven
milestones.tips: Skarmory, Aggron, Cradily, Excadrill, Archeops, Metagross (Lv 80-82; Hard Lv 84-86 with Gholdengo) in a Kitakami house after you become Champion. He gives a Beldum, and beating him opens Rayquaza at the Embedded Tower.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers; SoulGold docs: legendary locations; SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

milestones.name: Green in the Nameless Cave
milestones.tips: Chansey, Volcarona, Thundurus (Therian), Tapu Fini, Dragapult, Venusaur (Lv 85-87) on B2F of the Nameless Cave (the ROM stores her as Green; the same team, as Leaf, is a Title Defense challenger).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Nameless Cave B2F)

milestones.name: The spirits of the Vajra Pyramid
milestones.tips: On floor 4 three ghosts fight in turn (Lv 77, 78, 79; the last has Dragapult, Aegislash, Annihilape, Skeledirge, Gengar). This is the Hoopa quest: trade a Tinkaton in Rinto Village first, then explore the pyramid's depths as Champion.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Vajra Pyramid Floor 4); SoulGold docs: legendary locations (Hoopa)

milestones.name: Battle Café bosses
milestones.tips: The Route 50 Battle Café's hardest opponents: Nem (Sableye, Flutter Mane, Annihilape, Gholdengo, Gengar, Marshadow) and Simpli (Grimmsnarl, Palafin, Kyogre, Swampert, Dragapult, Kingambit), Lv 90, Lv 100 on Hard. Beating every regular café opponent once earns Diancie.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; SoulGold docs: trainers (Battle Cafe); SoulGold docs: legendary locations (Diancie)

milestones.name: Ho-Oh or Lugia
milestones.tips: After the Radio Tower you pick the Rainbow Wing (Ho-Oh, Tin Tower) or the Silver Wing (Lugia, Whirl Islands); the radio director gives the other after the Elite Four. Legends are boss fights with several HP bars, and a beaten boss is a sure catch.
milestones.source: soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Celebi (Ilex Forest)
milestones.tips: Solve all eight Ruins of Alph puzzles, then see Kurt and visit the Ilex shrine.
milestones.source: soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Mewtwo (Kitakami Border)
milestones.tips: In the Nameless Dungeon at the Kitakami Border, after the Elite Four (Rock Climb).
milestones.source: soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

steps.title: Optional level caps
steps.text: Caps (if turned on): 12, 19, 26, 34, 42, 45, 48, 55 for the Rocket takeover, 58, 62 until Ho-Oh/Lugia, 70 until the Champion.

steps.title: Innate abilities
steps.text: Pokémon gain extra innate abilities at Lv 75, 85 and 95; a bookcase in Elm's lab unlocks them early or turns them off.

steps.title: HMs need the HM and the badge
steps.text: Strength is from the Olivine café, Waterfall from the Ice Path, Rock Climb works after badge 8.

steps.title: Any starter from the casino
steps.text: The Goldenrod casino's gachapon sells starters from every generation (3000+ coins).

steps.title: Dratini in Blackthorn
steps.text: Blackthorn gives a Dratini; answer correctly and it knows Spacial Rend.

steps.title: Poké Balls, DexNav and a gift
steps.text: Once you have your first Poké Balls the DexNav unlocks, and Cherrygrove offers a choice of Alolan Rattata or Galarian Zigzagoon. The rival gives the Exp. Share before Violet City.
steps.source: SoulGold docs: FAQ; SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

steps.title: Classic or Hard
steps.text: Hard mode turns gym battles into double battles (unless a setting forces singles) and gives trainers without set moves smarter movesets as you progress. The guide lists both modes' top levels.

steps.title: Egg and Candy Jar
steps.text: After the first gym Elm's aide brings an egg and the Candy Jar, which banks surplus battle Exp. and turns it into Exp. Candy when used: handy to catch up without breaking a level cap.

steps.title: Hidden Grottos
steps.text: Look for odd paths behind trees: Route 32 has the first grotto (Lv 10: Applin, Paldean Wooper, Mareep, Misdreavus). Grottos refill daily, or at once with a Beckoning Bell (one free in Ilex Forest).

steps.title: Fossils from the Ruins
steps.text: Smash rocks in the Ruins of Alph for fossils and have the scientist in the nearby building revive them. Solving all eight puzzles later leads to Celebi.
steps.source: SoulGold docs: FAQ; SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

steps.title: The Odd Egg
steps.text: The rival's Odd Egg hatches into Bagon, Gible, Feebas, Riolu, Jangmo-o, Hisuian Zorua or Goomy.
steps.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

steps.title: Open Whitney's gym
steps.text: Her gym stays closed until you complete the quiz on the Radio Tower's first floor. Pick up the Coin Case in the Goldenrod Underground while you're there.

steps.title: The odd tree
steps.text: After the third badge, get the Squirtbottle from the flower shop next to the gym to wake the tree that blocks the way.

steps.title: Battle Factory after gym 3
steps.text: The Battle Factory opens after Whitney: rounds there pay for ability changes, IV feathers and Beckoning Bells, and after eight badges it also stocks Nuggets and Big Nuggets.

steps.title: Gyms 5-7 in any order
steps.text: Chuck, Jasmine and Pryce scale with your badges (Lv 42 at four, 45 at five, 48 at six); since 1.1.3 their Classic teams are slightly easier. The optional caps are 42, 45 and 48.
steps.source: ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table; soulgold.run changelog (1.1.3); SoulGold docs: FAQ

steps.title: Olivine's services
steps.text: Olivine's beach café sells nature mints; the top-right house's tutor master sells every tutor move for 44,444, then teachable from the summary screen.

steps.title: Trophies
steps.text: Over 100 trophies. The gentleman in the Route 40 house tracks them and rewards 15 (Shiny Genome), 30 (Ash-Greninja), 45 (Poipole), 60 (Eternal Floette), 75 (Zarude) and 100 (original-colour Magearna).

steps.title: After the takeover
steps.text: Clearing the Radio Tower gives the Mega Ring (press START on the move screen to Mega Evolve) and the choice of the Rainbow Wing (Ho-Oh) or the Silver Wing (Lugia). The cap is 55 for this event.
steps.source: SoulGold docs: FAQ; SoulGold docs: legendary locations

steps.title: Safari Zone areas
steps.text: Most regional forms live in Baoba's Safari Zone. Its second area opens before the Ice Path, the third after you leave Tohjo Falls.

steps.title: Egg move master
steps.text: Blackthorn's egg move master sells access to every egg move for 88,888, taught from the summary screen afterwards.

steps.title: Money
steps.text: A Pickup Pokémon sends finds to the bag even with a held item. Sell feathers and shards; from Goldenrod, Covet or Thief Route 35's Yanma for Wide Lenses (DexNav chains help). Nuggets at the Battle Factory after eight badges.

steps.title: Indigo Plateau mart
steps.text: The Pokémon Center mart at the Plateau sells every evolution stone, the Linking Cord, Peat Block and Black Augurite (since 1.2) and the two Charcadet armors: stock up on evolutions before the Elite Four.

steps.title: Before the Elite Four
steps.text: The optional cap is 70 until you become Champion. Will (Psychic), Koga (Poison), Bruno (Fighting) and Karen (Dark) are Lv 67-71, Lance's dragons up to 71; Ice and Fairy moves carry the final fight.
steps.source: SoulGold docs: FAQ; ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table

steps.title: The Dive questline
steps.text: After the Mt. Silver rival story, talk to your rival in their house: Cresselia at the Lake of Rage, then Darkrai at the Cherrygrove inn, then HM Dive (Kyogre and Groudon dive spots).
steps.source: SoulGold docs: FAQ; SoulGold docs: legendary locations

steps.title: Training for the postgame
steps.text: Kitakami has an Audino/Blissey trainer for 10,000. IVs: feathers (+5 each) and Hyper Training with Bottle Caps in Rinto Village. EV items are buffed and sold in Goldenrod; vitamins go past 100 EVs.

steps.title: Victini
steps.text: After becoming Champion talk to the old woman in the Kitakami Border house, then beat every gym leader rematch for Victini.

steps.title: Arceus
steps.text: Catch all 608 non-legendary, non-mythical Pokémon, then see Professor Oak on Radio Tower 2F. Since 1.2 the Paradox legends aren't needed for the Pokédex.

steps.title: Battle Café points
steps.text: Route 50's Battle Café sells legends for points: Galarian birds, the forces of nature and the Tapus at 5 each (the first force also gives the Reveal Glass); Koraidon or Miraidon at 25 once every other Paradox is caught.

secrets.text: Bill gives an Eevee or a Pikachu.
Cianwood gives a Gimmighoul.
A Tyrogue in Mt. Mortar.
Since 1.1.4 Cursola lives in the waters of Rinto Village.
Regirock in the Vajra Desert: bring a Tyranitar.
Regice on Snowtop Mountain (bring a Baxcalibur); Articuno is up there too (Rock Climb).
Registeel in the Railway Cave: bring a Kommo-o.
Regigigas on Mt. Silver, with all three Regis in the party.
Zapdos on top of the Olivine lighthouse after badge 8.
Moltres on Victory Road.
Heatran in Mt. Mortar.
Primal Dialga at the Spear Pillar.
Most Paradox Pokémon live on Meteor Island; the changed beasts come from the roaming trio.
Shadow Lugia: the Dark Crystal from the abandoned Rocket warehouse south of Route 33.
Latias and Latios in the Vajra temple; the Vajra Pyramid is a battle facility.
The Rocket Arcade pays money; 25 wins give Magearna.
Dream Garden is one of SoulGold's added areas, with Tohjo Pass, Route 50 and Meteor Island.
A choice of Alolan Rattata or Galarian Zigzagoon.
secrets.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

secrets.text: The rival's Odd Egg: Bagon, Gible, Feebas, Riolu, Jangmo-o, Hisuian Zorua or Goomy.
secrets.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

secrets.text: Hand fossils from smashed Ruins rocks to the scientist for the matching fossil Pokémon.
secrets.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

secrets.text: Steven gives a Beldum.
secrets.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

secrets.text: Elm's lab gives a Shiny Stone.
A Choice Band on Route 27, where the last Route Expert waits.
secrets.source: SoulGold docs: items; SoulGold docs: trainers

secrets.text: Someone in Ilex Forest gives a Beckoning Bell, which refreshes the Hidden Grottos.
Trade a Cottonee for a Pawmi.
secrets.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

secrets.text: Trade a Slowpoke for a Galarian Slowpoke.
secrets.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

secrets.text: Trade a Clefairy for a Honedge in the Dept. Store.
secrets.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

secrets.text: Trade a Zorua for a Rotom in the Route 39-Route 49 gatehouse.
secrets.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

secrets.text: Trade a Mareanie for a Hisuian Voltorb.

secrets.text: NPC trades can be shiny, at 12 times the usual odds: save first and check the trade animation.
A shiny starter shows a gold ball in Elm's case: save in front of it and soft reset.
Show a Rotom to the guard on the Goldenrod Apartment's first floor to open the basement with the form-changing appliances.
The Coin Case lies in the Goldenrod Underground; the casino gachapon behind the prize counter gives any generation's starter (3,000 coins or more; more coins, fewer duplicates).

Azelf at the Rock Climb spot in Mahogany Town.
Rayquaza at the Embedded Tower once you've beaten Steven in Kitakami.
Kyogre: surf south from Route 33, take the first left and dive.
Groudon in a small cave below a Route 50 dive spot.
Cresselia: after the Mt. Silver story see your rival, then the Hidden Power man at the lake, then its north-east corner.
Darkrai: show Cresselia to your rival, then enter the Cherrygrove inn with it and solve the inn's puzzle.

Shaymin in the Dream Garden, reached from Tohjo Falls.
Marshadow: with eight badges beat Elder Li again, then explore the Sprout Tower basement.
Dialga, Palkia and Giratina: solve all eight Ruins puzzles, bring Hoopa to Celebi's secret room and touch the back wall for the portals.
Cobalion through the Railway Cave's Route 33 exit; Terrakion in Dark Cave North; Virizion on Route 50.

notes.title: SoulGold 1.1.4 to 1.2.1
notes.text: A Johto-only remake on pokeemerald-expansion 1.15 (the official FAQ: no Kanto), using an unofficial port of Heart & Soul's assets. 132 areas and every generation's Pokémon; Classic and Hard modes. 1.1.4 added innate and night-lighting toggles; 1.2 (3 Oct 2026) and 1.2.1 (25 Oct 2026) are covered by the same guide.
notes.source: GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold README and releases; SoulGold docs: FAQ; soulgold.run changelog

notes.title: Mega Evolution
notes.text: Every Mega, with type-generic stones (Elm gives your starter's); new Megas for Typhlosion, Meowscarada and Primarina. Press START on the move screen to Mega Evolve.

notes.title: Features
notes.text: DexNav after the first Poké Balls, followers, daily hidden grottoes, a VS Seeker, feather fishing (IV training), a move relearner with a TM tab, Exp. Share before Violet, a Candy Jar after gym 1, shiny odds setting.

notes.title: The beasts
notes.text: Raikou, Entei and Suicune all roam after the Burned Tower; their shininess is rolled when they are released.

notes.title: No Kanto
notes.text: The ROM still carries Kanto map names and Kanto leaders' teams (Lt. Surge, Erika, Misty, Janine, Brock, Sabrina, Blue), but the game has no Kanto: of them only Blaine appears, at the Olivine port. Eight badges.
notes.source: SoulGold docs: FAQ; SoulGold docs: trainers; ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table

notes.title: Version 1.2
notes.text: Elite Four rematch and Title Defense teams adjusted; Paradox legends respawn after a Title Defense and no longer count for the Pokédex; Peat Block and Black Augurite sold at the Plateau; shiny parents raise egg odds; Audino gives more Exp.

notes.title: Version 1.2.1
notes.text: Grotto Pokémon can show as shiny when you enter; a battle status screen; box search by type; DexNav chains survive map changes; more Gen 8 egg moves at the egg tutor; Red and Blue Orbs added to the Plateau mart.

notes.title: Hard mode
notes.text: Gyms become double battles unless a setting forces singles, and trainers without set moves get smarter movesets as you progress. Most bosses have a separate Hard team, usually a level or two higher.
notes.source: SoulGold docs: FAQ; ROM SoulGold 1.2.1 trainer table

notes.title: Level caps
notes.text: Optional: 12, 19, 26, 34, 42, 45, 48, 55 (the Rocket takeover), 58, 62 (until you catch Ho-Oh or Lugia) and 70 (until you become Champion).

notes.title: In-game trades
notes.text: Pawmi for Cottonee (Violet), Galarian Slowpoke for Slowpoke (Azalea), Honedge for Clefairy (Goldenrod Dept. Store), Rotom for Zorua (Route 39/49 gate), Hisuian Voltorb for Mareanie (Olivine), Gabite for Dragonair (Blackthorn), Meltan for Tinkaton (Rinto). Traded Pokémon have 12x shiny odds.
notes.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon; SoulGold docs: shiny hunting

notes.title: Gift Pokémon
notes.text: Alolan Rattata or Galarian Zigzagoon (Cherrygrove), the Odd Egg (rival), fossils (Ruins of Alph), Eevee or Pikachu (Bill), Gimmighoul (Cianwood), Tyrogue (Kiyo), Dratini (Blackthorn), Beldum (Steven), every starter (casino gachapon) and the trophy rewards (Route 40).
notes.source: SoulGold docs: gift and trade Pokémon

notes.title: Trophy rewards
notes.text: The Route 40 gentleman: 15 trophies Shiny Genome (makes one Pokémon shiny), 30 Ash-Greninja, 45 Poipole, 60 Eternal Floette, 75 Zarude, 100 original-colour Magearna. All can be shiny.

notes.title: Hidden Grottos
notes.text: A grotto holds a Pokémon 60% of the time (two perfect IVs and its Hidden Ability), a common item 32%, its special item 8%. They refill daily or with a Beckoning Bell. Grottos: Routes 32, 33, 35, 38, 44, 47, Ilex Forest, Goldenrod Shore, Vajra Desert, Lake of Rage.

notes.title: Shiny hunting
notes.text: Odds 1/256 by default (1/512 or 1/1024 in the options); no shiny locks. DexNav streaks of 50 and 100 help; shiny parents raise egg odds (no Masuda Method); the beasts' shininess is fixed when the Burned Tower releases them.
notes.source: SoulGold docs: shiny hunting; SoulGold docs: FAQ

notes.title: HMs
notes.text: No HM moves to teach: owning the HM and its badge is enough, and Fly works from the Pokégear map. Strength comes from the Olivine café, Waterfall from the Ice Path, Rock Climb after badge 8, Dive late in the postgame.
notes.source: SoulGold docs: FAQ; SoulGold docs: legendary locations

notes.title: Title Defense
notes.text: After the Elite Four rematch you defend the title against a changing challenger (Lance, Steven, Leaf, or a Johto leader with a legend) instead of the same Champion every time.
notes.source: GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold README; SoulGold docs: trainers (Title Defense)

notes.title: Paradox Pokémon
notes.text: Most Paradox Pokémon live on Meteor Island in South Johto; Chien-Pao is deep in the Ice Path and Chi-Yu in the Battle Café's fountain. Since 1.2 the Paradox legends respawn after a Title Defense.
notes.source: SoulGold docs: legendary locations; soulgold.run changelog (v1.2)

notes.title: Battle Café legends
notes.text: Route 50's Battle Café sells Galarian Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres, Tornadus, Thundurus, Landorus and Enamorus, and the four Tapus for 5 points each; Koraidon or Miraidon for 25 once you have every other Paradox. Clear every regular opponent once for Diancie.

notes.title: Uxie, Mesprit and Azelf
notes.text: Each sits at a Rock Climb spot: Uxie on Route 30 by the Berry Man, Mesprit on Route 47 by the last bridge, Azelf in Mahogany Town.

notes.title: The Regis
notes.text: Braille puzzles: Regirock in Vajra Desert West (bring Tyranitar), Regice on Snowtop Mountain (Baxcalibur), Registeel in the Railway Cave (Kommo-o). All three in the party open Regigigas on Mt. Silver.

notes.title: The postgame rival chain
notes.text: Finish the Mt. Silver rival story (Jirachi), visit your rival's house: Cresselia at the Lake of Rage, then Darkrai at the Cherrygrove inn, then HM Dive opens Kyogre (south of Route 33) and Groudon (Route 50).
notes.source: SoulGold docs: legendary locations; SoulGold docs: FAQ

notes.title: Ruins of Alph legends
notes.text: All eight puzzles (four sliders, four walls: Escape Rope, Water Stone, Flash, Ho-Oh) lead to the GS Ball for Celebi via Kurt. With Hoopa in the party the same secret room opens portals to Dialga, Palkia and Giratina.

notes.title: Times of day
notes.text: Morning 06:00-10:00, day 10:00-19:00, evening 19:00-20:00, night 20:00-06:00 (in-game time): it decides day and night evolutions and encounters.
